# WebRTC Gotchas

> Known WebRTC patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [profile-level-id=42e01f caps you at 1280x720, and a hardware decoder answers a bigger picture with silence](h264-level-vs-desktop-resolution.md): The `1f` everyone copies is Level 3.1, MaxFS 3600 macroblocks, which is exactly 1280x720. A screen-share or remote-desktop stream that declares it and then encodes a real display is advertising a smaller picture than it sends: 1280x1024 is 42% over, 1080p is 127% over, 4K is 800% over. A hardware decoder sizes itself from the negotiated level before any bitstream arrives, is handed something larger, and produces no frames while raising no error and not falling back to software. The session is fully connected with bytesReceived climbing and framesDecoded stuck at 0, and it takes the mouse with it because a never-decoded video has videoWidth 0. Reproduces on a 1280x1024 terminal and not on a 1280x720 laptop, so it reads as "certain machines are broken". Raising the level is safe: profileLevelIDMatches compares only profile_idc and profile_iop, never the level byte. HIGH.
- [In a paired signaling relay, evicting a duplicate peer tears down the whole pairing, not just that peer](relay-eviction-ends-the-pairing.md): Closing the incumbent fires ITS close handler, which is teardown, which closes the pairing, which closes the other side too. So "replace the duplicate" does not hand the session to the newcomer: the endpoint sees its channel close, reads it as a failed host, and the session ends for everybody while the newcomer joins something being destroyed underneath them. Every piece is individually defensible, and the natural test asserts the eviction and stops, so a passing test can be documenting the bug. Refuse the newcomer instead (the teardown guard then returns early because it was never installed), or make teardown asymmetric so one side is the session and the other is a participant. Tell a rival from a reconnect by readyState. HIGH.
- [One-to-many screen share needs no SFU: a single local track fans out to N PeerConnections](one-to-many-without-an-sfu.md): pion's TrackLocalStaticSample keeps a slice of bindings, Bind appends one per PeerConnection, and WriteSample writes them all, so N viewers cost N RTP senders and still exactly one capture, one conversion and one encode. On desktop capture that is not an optimisation but the only workable arrangement, because DXGI Desktop Duplication permits one duplication per output, so per-viewer host processes cannot work at all. Route every viewer's PLI through one rate-limited gate or ten viewers joining together become ten encoder rebuilds. Video fans out, input does not: decide the driver model explicitly. Reach for an SFU only for per-viewer bitrate adaptation, viewer counts that saturate the endpoint's uplink, or a publisher that cannot hold N connections. MEDIUM.
